01-protecting-a-qubit: Encoding spreads one unknown state across a joint system; it does not clone it.
A syndrome must reveal the error sector without revealing the logical amplitudes.
State the error family and preserve reference correlations before calling a recovery successful.
02-correctable-errors: Exact recovery requires the environment to learn no logical information, including coherence.
The Knill–Laflamme condition is both an impossibility test and a route to a recovery construction.
Correctability extends to an operator span, but a realistic noise channel may also contain terms outside that span.
03-stabilizer-codes: Independent commuting Pauli checks define a code of dimension 2^(n−r).
Syndromes are anticommutation records, independent of logical amplitudes.
A short generator list can certify correction without constructing every codeword.
04-css-codes: Classical syndromes remove the codeword and retain a linear signature of the error.
CSS construction requires HₓH𝓏ᵀ=0, not just two individually good classical codes.
The Steane code encodes quantum superpositions over classical cosets.
05-logical-operators: A zero syndrome identifies the centralizer, not necessarily the identity action.
Distance is the minimum nontrivial logical Pauli weight; arbitrary t-error correction needs 2t<d.
Constructing one logical operator proves an upper bound; proving distance also needs a lower bound.
06-syndromes-and-decoding: A parity circuit must preserve coherence inside each eigenspace.
Decoding chooses a logical equivalence class under an explicit noise model.
Noisy syndrome histories require temporal information and boundary handling.
07-surface-codes: Local stabilizer checks detect chain endpoints; they do not reveal a unique error path.
Logical failure occurs when error and recovery combine into a nontrivial path class.
Toric and planar boundary conditions change logical counts and resource estimates.
08-fault-tolerant-operations: Fault propagation has direction and Pauli type; a target Z can spread backward through CNOT.
Logical correctness and fault containment require separate arguments.
Verified ancillas, flags, and repeated checks need circuit-specific fault proofs.
09-universal-logical-computation: Clifford operations are useful but need an additional resource for universality.
Gate injection must account for every measurement branch and its conditional correction.
Distillation trades input states and protected operations for output accuracy; correlations and yield matter.
10-thresholds-and-resources: Threshold arguments depend on a declared local noise model and fault-tolerant gadget construction.
A computation needs a total error budget with consistent per-round or per-gate units.
Resource estimates must include yield, time, factories, and omitted architecture costs—not only data qubits.
